docs.title: Course Description
docs.text: CW 10 is an introductory general education course exploring the art and craft of literary writing. Creative writing is more than decorative verse or prose: it is an intellectual & artistic tool for shaping language to capture complex human truths, emotions, & ideas. Through creative exercises & critical dialogue, students will examine how creative writing serves as both a compelling art form & a rigorous mode of scholarly inquiry.

docs.title: Course Structure
docs.text:
This course will employ face-to-face and asynchronous modes of learning.

We meet in-person at:

  • THV CAL 211 TTh 11:30-1:00
  • THX CAL 212 TTh 2:30-4:00

docs.title: Course Learning Outcomes
docs.text:
• Analyze creative writing as a distinct form of knowledge creation and scholarly discourse.
  • Apply key techniques and creative strategies used across literary genres.
  • Produce original creative works that engage the imagination and contribute to local literary communities in the Philippines.

docs.title: Welcome to Creative Writing
docs.text: When Socrates said, "ὁ δὲ ἀνεξέταστος βίος οὐ βιωτὸς ἀνθρώπῳ," it is more less a polite philosophical invitation & more an intellectual dare. It asks us to unpack our unexamined assumptions into the harsh light of critical thought knowing full well that once we crack open the lid, there is no way to seal it again. You took this course because you want to open that can: curious of what's inside: a sprung snake-in-a-can, a Mentos soda geyser, or even to find nothing inside.

docs.title: Quick Start: Why Are You Here?
docs.text:
• You think this is an easy UNO and the prof is UNOABLE (only one way to find out). Do you like surprises?
  • You want a respite from the humdrum of maths and sciences.
  • Therapy is expensive: Processing unresolved childhood trauma or that bizarre interaction at the grocery store is significantly cheaper when disguised as a "flash fiction exercise."
  • To sound interesting at parties: Saying "I'm working on a manuscript" sounds substantially more sophisticated than admitting you spent four hours arguing on Reddit or overthinking a text message.
  • To justify hours of staring at the wall: In a normal class, staring blankly out the window for 20 minutes looks like slacking off. In a creative writing workshop, it’s called "ruminating on narrative voice."

Why are you here?

docs.title: B5 - The World is Your Talaba & You're a Talangka
Broadening your intellectual and cultural horizons
docs.text: You might be used to reading standard literary classics chosen simply because they’re considered canonical, meaning "important," without much discussion on how they actually work. In our creative writing classroom, we look at literature differently. We use stories, essays, and poems—from the Philippines and around the world—as inspiration and practical guides. By exploring these texts together, my goal is to widen your reading perspectives and show you how specific techniques bring writing to life so you can apply those lessons to your own craft.

docs.title: I30 Incurable obsession with the local albularyo
Ignite your Critical & Imaginative Thinking
docs.text: Looking at literature through a writer's lens invites you to rethink how language, reading, and storytelling work. Instead of just analyzing a text from a distance, you’ll interact with it directly—writing back to it, writing alongside it, and reshaping ideas in your own voice. I want to encourage you to push past familiar habits, experiment with language in unexpected ways, and discover fresh ways of seeing the world.

docs.title: N1 Neon Glare Over Rainy Pavement
Nurture a passion for learning and craft
docs.text: As you experiment with different poetic and narrative techniques, you'll naturally sharpen your aesthetic instincts and build a deeper appreciation for the written word. We’ll nurture this growth together through workshop sessions and peer reviews. These collaborative, guided conversations are designed to give you constructive feedback, spark new ideas, and build a supportive community where we all learn from one another.

docs.title: Grounded in Intellectual & Moral Integrity
docs.text: Your voice matters, and I want you to take genuine pride in creating work that is authentically yours. Throughout the course, we’ll pay close attention to how readers interpret language and how subtle choices shape meaning. Learning to navigate these nuances helps you take thoughtful ownership of your words, honoring both your creative vision and the audience reading your work.

docs.title: O68 Out-of-body Experience on Aisle Four
Orchestrating Community Growth & Social Impact
docs.text: Writing doesn't happen in a vacuum. By immersing ourselves in the work of contemporary writers shaping Philippine culture, we’ll explore how literature responds to social realities, highlights injustices, and contributes to our national identity. I hope this course helps you see how your own creative voice fits into the broader 21st-century Philippine landscape, empowering you to write with intention, empathy, and purpose.

docs.title: Read
docs.text:
Read the assigned texts at least once before coming to class and bring your own copies of the text to class. You will be gently asked to go to the library and read if you admit that you have failed to read (or provide answers that reveal that you have failed to read) the text under discussion. This breaks my heart.

You will never learn how to write if you don't read.

docs.title: Ethos
docs.text: This course operates as a serious artistic community. Writing will be treated as craft, labor, and risk. Respect—for the work, the writer, and the room—is non-negotiable. We are here to sharpen each other, not to perform expertise or score points.

docs.title: Class Harmony
docs.text: This class has a zero-tolerance for bullying: physical, verbal, cyber--none of it. There is only one designated bully in this class: me.

docs.title: Absences
docs.text:
• You are allowed six cuts, hit your seventh & you'll get a 5.0 if you didn't drop this course. I don't need to know why you missed class unless it is a fairly entertaining story. It is your responsibility though to update yourself with the class activities you missed while you were gone.
  • If you are sick, it is advisable to stay at home and rest and avoid making this class a superspreader event. You do not need to send a medical certificate to prove you are sick.

docs.title: Tardiness
docs.text: I do not mind students coming in late (the campus is huge and sometimes the wait is long for Ikot jeeps) but I mind if your entrance creates a disturbance in class discussion. Make your arrival as quiet as a mouse and as inconspicuous as a pork barrel insertion as possible.

docs.title: What if I'm the one who's late?
docs.text: Wait for me for 15 minutes...or more. Please check Discord if I'm stuck in traffic or helping an elderly woman cross the street. At any rate, class is not cancelled unless I explicitly announce it.

docs.title: Communication
docs.text:
• Follow standard hours of communication.
  • Introduce yourself in your emails & change your username to Discord to your government name or class nickname.
  • But, you can always send a message to me on Discord & I will respond as soon as I can (no ungodly hours please).

docs.title: Extra Credit
docs.text: I do not, & will not, give special projects to students seeking higher grades.

docs.title: Academic Integrity
docs.text:
• This is a creative writing class. NO AI submissions. Have some self-respect.
  • Academic integrity is expected of all students. Any act of intellectual dishonesty (especially plagiarism) will be penalized with either suspension or expulsion, depending on the degree of the offense. Refer to the 2012 Code of Student Conduct. You may consult this for a more detailed definition of plagiarism and how to avoid it.

docs.title: On Workshops
docs.text:
Be direct, clear, & honest about what is or isn't working on the page. However, there is a distinct line between rigorous feedback and deliberate malice—do not cross it. Focus on the text, not the person behind it, & frame your observations so the writer leaves equipped to revise, not discouraged from writing. & absolutely: NO CRYING.

Cry after class. & don't let anyone see it.

docs.title: Deadlines
docs.text:
• You have a one-day extension after a set deadline to submit your work, but I will apply a minus .5 to your grade.
  • Any submissions beyond the period will no longer be accepted.
  • Exceptions: a close relative dies; a best friend dies; a pet dies; you die.
  • Deadlines will only be shifted for reasons of force majeure, or if I decide to change my mind. At any rate, you will hear about it.
  • On workshops, if you miss to send your work on time, you not only get a 5.0 for that exercise, you also miss your chance to be workshopped.
  • So please, align your social & intimate lives with this class's deadlines & prepare & plan ahead.

docs.title: Data Policy
docs.text:
• UP Diliman’s Data Privacy Policy will be strictly observed in this course. While you are free to communicate with each other on social media or other personal platforms, all official/formal communications for this course (submissions, questions to the instructor, workshops, etc) will only be done through official channels (that includes our official Discord server), using your UP mail account.
  • Over the course of the semester, you may become privy to personal, private information about your classmates or your instructor, including but not limited to their contact information, medical history, gender preferences, etc. Do not share any of this information to anyone outside of the course. This is very important as many of you will be sharing and writing personal stuff, and maybe trauma, in your writing. What happens in CW 10 stays in CW 10!!

docs.title: Me
docs.text:
My name is Michael Balili. You can call me Michael, or by my nickname, Mickey. My concentration is poetry.

You can learn more about my works on my website.

You can email me at mtbalili@up.edu.ph.

docs.title: KALBaryo
docs.text: Since the Faculty Center burned down 10 years ago (imagine that!), CAL still has no building to call its own. I am heartbroken to tell you we won't have physical spaces to hold consultations. We can do this through Zoom or Discord (please email and schedule) or informally, after class while we're walking down the staircase (elevator-pitch style) or if you want a longer kwentuhan, inside the Gonzalo Gonzales Reading Room (again, send an email and schedule).

docs.title: Consultation
docs.text:
• You may pitch your ideas or go over your concepts to me before committing them on paper. Think of this opportunity as a place to fine-tune ideas & concepts before writing your draft. Take advantage of it.

  • There will also be time set aside during the semester when you can schedule a one-on-one consultation with me. The consultation can be through Zoom or Discord, or if you are unable to commit to a synchronous meeting, through email or through Discord.

  • During the consultation, I may check up on you & discuss your performance in class, or inquire if you have been having difficulties with the sessions or readings. However, the bulk of your discussion will be about your plans for the workshop draft submission.

docs.title: Class & Workshop Participation - 40%
docs.text:
Do not just take space. You must be in CW 10 physically & mentally.

You are expected to contribute to the overall quality of discussions & workshop sessions, which means that you should come to class having read the assigned text at least once and having thought about the readings & ready to offer your own insights, comments, & questions.

docs.title: Writing Exercises - 20%
docs.text: There will be a few writing exercises in between readings.

docs.title: Midterm CNF - 20%
docs.text: You will be assigned to read a whole book & write a creative non-fiction piece about the book & your life. Details will be posted on the Google Classroom submission bin.

docs.title: Revised Manuscript & Folio - 40%
docs.text: This is your revised work following your workshop. Your group will collate all your works, produce & publish your revised works as a physical book; however, while this is a collaborative project, your individual contribution will be evaluated separately.

docs.title: Group Assignments
docs.text: I am teaching two CW 10 classes this term so please don't mind the other section & focus your attention to your assigned group. There are group rooms in Discord & you should use these to connect with your groupmates. I hope that, after the semester is over, you have also found lifelong friends in this class.

docs.title: Metaphors
docs.text:
The best way to learn how metaphors work is by listening to songs because music strips imagery down to its purest emotional rhythm, demonstrating how two completely unrelated concepts can fuse to create instant meaning.

In this playlist, listen to how lyricists select, sustain, and distort imagery within the tight constraints of a melody: active, living engines of emotion and narrative tension.
